e: In Saxony-Anhalt, Tobias Rausch from the AfD is elected speaker of Saxony-Anhalt's state parliament. The party's first in such position and the first time a far-right party has held such a post in the country since 1945.
A bus carrying tourists to a festival in Munich overturns, killing two people and injuring eight others.
The town of Heidenau in Saxony bans future Holocaust memorial plaques with support from the AfD and CDU.
A wave of strikes are held in schools nationwide by student protesting against the government's plans to reintroduce conscription.
An F-16 fighter jet of the United States Air Force crashes near Spangdahlem Air Base. The pilot ejects safely.
A woman is injured in an antisemitic attack in Berlin.
Charlotte Knobloch, a Jewish leader and Holocaust survivor, receives a death threat following a call to ban the AfD.
An explosion near a train station injures two people in Augsburg.
Germany orders the closure of the Russian consulate and cultural center in Berlin after it finds the Russian government responsible for the 2026 Leipzig Airport drone attack.
Two people are killed in an incident of domestic violence at a school in Gosen-Neu Zittau.
Two employees at Frankfurt Airport are reported to have died from the first outbreak of aviation-acquired malaria in Germany since 2023.
Germany approves a large overhaul of its intelligence agencies, granting them vast new powers to conduct clandestine operations and combat external threats, especially Russian hybrid warfare.

The Hanseatic Higher Regional Court in Hamburg convicts seven members and one supporter of the "Last Defense Wave" extremist group and sentences them to prison for attempted murder, arson, aggravated assault, and being members of a terrorist organisation for planning and carrying out arson and bomb attacks on asylum seeker shelters.
An attempted drone attack blamed by the German government on Russia is carried out on a Ukrainian aircraft in Leipzig/Halle Airport.
A small plane carrying two people crashes into a house in Ganderkesee.

One person is killed and 29 others are injured in a vehicle-ramming and stabbing attack near the Christopher Street Day in Berlin. The 21-year-old male suspect is shot and killed by police the next day after rushing at officers with a knife in Spandau, Berlin.
A Munich court imprisons an Iraqi couple who were members of Islamic State for enslaving and raping Yazidi girls.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz announces that the Trump administration agreed to the sale of Tomahawk missiles to Germany.
The Alternative for Germany (AfD) holds its party congress in Erfurt. Tino Chrupalla and Alice Weidel are re-elected as party-leaders.
Prosecutors in Hesse arrest a German–Rwandan national on suspicion of complicity in the 1994 Rwandan genocide.
A shooting in Stade kills six people. Police detain a male suspect.
Almost the entire Deutsche Bahn railway network shuts down for two hours as part of scheduled maintenance on a communications system, triggering major transport disruptions.
Two freight trains collide in Munich, killing one person.
Germany and Poland sign a defense cooperation agreement.

The medieval manuscript of Gaude Mater Polonia, a ring of Polish King Sigismund the Old, and a collection of miniature model trains from a pre-war museum in Warsaw, all looted by Germany from Poland during World War II, are repatriated by Germany.

Hotel Zum Hirschen in Lam, Bavaria responds to an Israeli family attempting to make a reservation through Booking.com with: "Sorry, there are no Jews allowed in our hotel." Booking.com removes the hotel from its platform following backlash, and the hotel subsequently apologizes for the message.
The Public Prosecutor General arrests a Chinese couple in Munich on suspicion of spying for Chinese intelligence.
Germany finishes 23rd at Eurovision 2026 in Austria.
In Baden-Württemberg, Cem Özdemir becomes the first Minister-President of Turkish background.
A 17-year old male is arrested on suspicion of plotting to carry out terrorist attacks in Hamburg on behalf of Islamic State.
A car plows into a crowd in Grimmaische Strasse in Leipzig, killing two people and injuring 22 others.
A Kazakh national is arrested in Germany on suspicion of spying for Russia.
A wooden structure containing anti-semitic symbols is found outside the Eggenfelden tax office.
Three people, including two children, are killed and another is seriously injured after high winds cause a tree to fall onto an Easter egg hunt in Mittelangeln, Schleswig-Holstein.
A nightclub burns down in Kehl, Baden-Württemberg. All 750 people inside are evacuated, three of whom are treated for shock.

Germany drops out of defending Israel in the International Court of Justice's genocide case against Israel, citing their need to defend themselves in a separate case launched against them by Nicaragua.
German economic crisis: Lufthansa pilots organize a 48-hour strike over ongoing pension dispute, causing major delays at all German airports.
A meteorite strikes a roof of a house in Koblenz, Rhineland-Palatinate. No one is injured.

A court in Berlin convicts a Syrian national for carrying out a antisemitic knife attack at the Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe that injured one person in 2025 and sentences him to 13 years' imprisonment.
A court in Cologne issues an injunction against the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution's designation of the AfD as an extremist organization pending a judicial review.
